idiom_name: Promises and async/await over the libuv event loop
implementation_notes: Node's event loop is the completion dispatcher: libuv offloads I/O to the kernel, and when an operation completes its callback is queued for the poll phase, while promises wrap the same completion into a value that async functions await. No dispatcher can be written by hand in user code - the classic proactor roles are absorbed, and handlers are the continuations after await. Raw callback APIs and the (err, result) convention still appear when wrapping older modules, and streams remain callback-shaped because one connection produces many completions.
pitfalls: Any long synchronous computation blocks the single JavaScript thread and delays every pending completion; move heavy work to worker_threads or another process.
A rejected promise nobody handles surfaces as an unhandledRejection, and promises have no cancellation: the underlying operation needs an AbortController signal.
File-system and DNS work runs on libuv's thread pool (four threads by default), so saturating it stalls otherwise fast asynchronous file I/O.
Promise.race and its siblings leave handlers attached to the losing pending promise, so repeatedly racing a long-lived promise accumulates handlers.
